page.title: Google
page.subtitle: Federate McHarbor login to Google accounts. Supports both personal Google accounts and Google Workspace (set the Workspace Domain field to restrict to one tenant via the OIDC hd= hint). Admin group fetching is available for Workspace tenants via a service account with domain-wide delegation.
page.registerHint: Add a provider from the host's Settings > Security > Identity Providers page and pick "Google" as the provider_type.

help.client_id: OAuth 2.0 client ID from the Google Cloud console (APIs & Services > Credentials > your Web application OAuth client).
help.client_secret: OAuth client secret issued by Google. Stored encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM).
help.domain: Optional Google Workspace hosted domain (e.g. example.com). When set, the plugin passes it as the hd= query parameter so only accounts from that Workspace can sign in. Leave empty to allow personal Google accounts.
help.scopes: Space-separated OAuth scopes. Defaults to openid profile email. Add https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.group.readonly to enable admin group fetching via the Directory API.
help.service_account_json: Optional: contents of a Google service-account JSON key file with domain-wide delegation. Required for Admin SDK group fetching. Stored encrypted at rest.
help.delegated_user_email: Optional: the Workspace admin user the service account impersonates (e.g. admin@example.com). Required when service_account_json is set.
help.delegated_user_access_token: Optional: manually-issued Google API access token to use for Admin SDK calls. Use this until v1.1 ships RS256 JWT signing for service-account assertions.
help.user_email_for_lookup: Optional: email of the user to look up groups for. Most operators leave this blank and let the host pass the authenticated user's email at runtime.

guide.title: Set up Google sign-in in McHarbor
guide.subtitle: Create an OAuth 2.0 Web application client in the Google Cloud console, then optionally configure a service account for Admin SDK group fetching.

step1.title: Create or select a Google Cloud project
step1.body: Open the Google Cloud console and either pick an existing project or create a new one dedicated to McHarbor. Note the project ID — you'll reference it when configuring the OAuth consent screen.

step2.title: Configure the OAuth consent screen
step2.body: Under APIs & Services > OAuth consent screen, set the user type (Internal for Google Workspace, External otherwise), the support email, and the app name. Add the scopes you need: openid, profile, email (always), and https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.group.readonly (only if you want group fetching).

step3.title: Create an OAuth Web client
step3.body: Under APIs & Services > Credentials > Create credentials > OAuth client ID, pick Application type: Web application. Under Authorized redirect URIs, add the McHarbor callback URL shown on the provider edit page — the host appends /api/identity-providers/callback to your McHarbor base URL. Copy the Client ID and Client Secret that Google shows into the matching fields on the provider form.

step4.title: (Workspace only) Set the Workspace Domain
step4.body: If you want to restrict sign-in to a single Google Workspace tenant, paste the tenant's primary domain (e.g. example.com) into the Workspace Domain field. The plugin will pass it as the hd= query parameter to Google's login page. Leave the field empty to accept personal Google accounts.

step5.title: Test the connection
step5.body: Back in McHarbor, click "Test connection" on the provider form. A green result means the OIDC discovery document resolved and the OAuth client authenticated successfully against accounts.google.com — the configuration is valid.

step6.title: (Workspace only) Create a service account for Admin SDK
step6.body: Under IAM & Admin > Service Accounts > Create service account, give it a name like "mcharbor-admin-groups" and grant it the role Service Account User. Under Keys > Add key > Create new key, pick JSON and save the file — paste its entire contents into the Service Account JSON field on the provider form.

step7.title: (Workspace only) Enable domain-wide delegation
step7.body: In the Google Workspace admin console (admin.google.com) under Security > API controls > Domain-wide delegation, add the service account's client_id and the scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.group.readonly. Then set the Delegated User Email field on the provider form to the Workspace admin email the service account will impersonate (e.g. admin@example.com). Save the provider — McHarbor will use the delegated identity to fetch group membership on demand.
